title: Print all the guide says, or some
statement: Whether everything a lesson's guide says aloud must also be printed is unsettled: printing it all clutters the screen, while a read-along rule allows nothing spoken that isn't printed.
detail: A reading course's index of contradictions records this as undecided: feedback dated 2026-08-06 says not everything the guide says needs to be on screen or it will be cluttered, while the repository's read-along rule, enforced by a validator, allows nothing spoken that is not printed. The course's distilled audio rules take the first side: they print the lines that carry the lesson, leave the rest as audio, and cover the unprinted lines with captions.

evidence.quote: not everything Scout says needs to be on screen or it will be cluttered. This repo's read-along rule: nothing is spoken that is not printed, enforced by a validator.
Not everything Scout says is printed (stamp the load-bearing lines; the rest is audio) — and captions cover the unprinted (below).
